cards.flavorText: Explosive substances coat the shell on its back. Enemies that dare attack it will be blown away by an immense detonation.

cards.name: Scorbunny
cards.flavorText: It has special pads on the backs of its feet, and one on its nose. Once it's raring to fight, these pads radiate tremendous heat.

cards.name: Scorbunny
cards.flavorText: A warm-up of running around gets fire energy coursing through this Pokémon's body. Once that happens, it's ready to fight at full power.

cards.name: Raboot
cards.flavorText: It kicks berries right off the branches of trees and then juggles them with its feet, practicing its footwork.

cards.name: Raboot
cards.flavorText: Its thick and fluffy fur protects it from the cold and enables it to use hotter fire moves.

cards.name: Cinderace
cards.flavorText: It's skilled at both offense and defense, and it gets pumped up when cheered on. But if it starts showboating, it could put itself in a tough spot.

cards.name: Cinderace
cards.flavorText: It juggles a pebble with its feet, turning it into a burning soccer ball. Its shots strike opponents hard and leave them scorched.

cards.name: Cinderace
cards.flavorText: It juggles a pebble with its feet, turning it into a burning soccer ball. Its shots strike opponents hard and leave them scorched.

cards.name: Sizzlipede
cards.flavorText: It stores flammable gas in its body and uses it to generate heat. The yellow sections on its belly get particularly hot.

cards.name: Sizzlipede
cards.flavorText: It stores flammable gas in its body and uses it to generate heat. The yellow sections on its belly get particularly hot.

cards.name: Centiskorch
cards.flavorText: When it heats up, its body temperature reaches about 1,500 degrees Fahrenheit. It lashes its body like a whip and launches itself at enemies.

cards.name: Shellder
cards.flavorText: It swims facing backward by opening and closing its two-piece shell. It is surprisingly fast.

cards.name: Cloyster
cards.flavorText: Its shell is extremely hard. It cannot be shattered, even with a bomb. The shell opens only when it is attacking.

cards.name: Krabby
cards.flavorText: It can be found near the sea. The large pincers grow back if they are torn out of their sockets.

cards.name: Krabby
cards.flavorText: It can be found near the sea. The large pincers grow back if they are torn out of their sockets.

cards.name: Kingler
cards.flavorText: The large and hard pincer has 10,000-horsepower strength. However, being so big, it is unwieldy to move.

cards.name: Goldeen
cards.flavorText: Its dorsal and pectoral fins are strongly developed like muscles. It can swim at a speed of five knots.

cards.name: Goldeen
cards.flavorText: Its dorsal, pectoral, and tail fins wave elegantly in water. That is why it is known as the Water Dancer.

cards.name: Seaking
cards.flavorText: Using its horn, it bores holes in riverbed boulders, making nests to prevent its eggs from washing away.

cards.name: Lapras
cards.flavorText: A smart and kindhearted Pokémon, it glides across the surface of the sea while its beautiful song echoes around it.

cards.name: Qwilfish
cards.flavorText: The small spikes covering its body developed from scales. They inject a toxin that causes fainting.

cards.name: Mantine
cards.flavorText: If it builds up enough speed swimming, it can jump out above the waves and glide for over 300 feet.

cards.name: Sobble
cards.flavorText: When scared, this Pokémon cries. Its tears pack the chemical punch of 100 onions, and attackers won't be able to resist weeping.

cards.name: Sobble
cards.flavorText: When scared, this Pokémon cries. Its tears pack the chemical punch of 100 onions, and attackers won't be able to resist weeping.

cards.name: Drizzile
cards.flavorText: A clever combatant, this Pokémon battles using water balloons created with moisture secreted from its palms.

cards.name: Drizzile
cards.flavorText: A clever combatant, this Pokémon battles using water balloons created with moisture secreted from its palms.

cards.name: Inteleon
cards.flavorText: It has many hidden capabilities, such as fingertips that can shoot water and a membrane on its back that it can use to glide through the air.

cards.name: Inteleon
cards.flavorText: It has many hidden capabilities, such as fingertips that can shoot water and a membrane on its back that it can use to glide through the air.

cards.name: Chewtle
cards.flavorText: It starts off battles by attacking with its rock-hard horn, but as soon as the opponent flinches, this Pokémon bites down and never lets go.

cards.name: Drednaw
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon rapidly extends its retractable neck to sink its sharp fangs into distant enemies and take them down.

cards.name: Cramorant
cards.flavorText: It's so strong that it can knock out some opponents in a single hit, but it also may forget what it's battling midfight.

cards.name: Snom
cards.flavorText: It eats snow that piles up on the ground. The more snow it eats, the bigger and more impressive the spikes on its back grow.

cards.name: Frosmoth
cards.flavorText: It shows no mercy to any who desecrate fields and mountains. It will fly around on its icy wings, causing a blizzard to chase offenders away.

cards.name: Pikachu
cards.flavorText: Pikachu that can generate powerful electricity have cheek sacs that are extra soft and super stretchy.

cards.name: Raichu
cards.flavorText: Its long tail serves as a ground to protect itself from its own high-voltage power.

cards.name: Chinchou
cards.flavorText: On the dark ocean floor, its only means of communication is its constantly flashing lights.

cards.name: Chinchou
cards.flavorText: Its antennae, which evolved from a fin, have both positive and negative charges flowing through them.

cards.name: Lanturn
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon flashes a bright light that blinds its prey. This creates an opening for it to deliver an electrical attack.

cards.name: Joltik
cards.flavorText: Joltik can be found clinging to other Pokémon. It's soaking up static electricity because it can't produce a charge on its own.

cards.name: Galvantula
cards.flavorText: It launches electrified fur from its abdomen as its means of attack. Opponents hit by the fur could be in for three full days and nights of paralysis.

cards.name: Yamper
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon is very popular as a herding dog in the Galar region. As it runs, it generates electricity from the base of its tail.

cards.name: Yamper
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon is very popular as a herding dog in the Galar region. As it runs, it generates electricity from the base of its tail.

cards.name: Boltund
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon generates electricity and channels it into its legs to keep them going strong. Boltund can run nonstop for three full days.

cards.name: Boltund
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon generates electricity and channels it into its legs to keep them going strong. Boltund can run nonstop for three full days.

cards.name: Pincurchin
cards.flavorText: It feeds on seaweed, using its teeth to scrape it off rocks. Electric current flows from the tips of its spines.

cards.name: Morpeko
cards.flavorText: As it eats the seeds stored up in its pocket-like pouches, this Pokémon is not just satisfying its constant hunger. It's also generating electricity.

cards.name: Galarian Ponyta
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon will look into your eyes and read the contents of your heart. If it finds evil there, it promptly hides away.

cards.name: Galarian Rapidash
cards.flavorText: Brave and prideful, this Pokémon dashes airily through the forest, its steps aided by the psychic power stored in the fur on its fetlocks.

cards.name: Gastly
cards.flavorText: Born from gases, anyone would faint if engulfed by its gaseous body, which contains poison.

cards.name: Haunter
cards.flavorText: Its tongue is made of gas. If licked, its victim starts shaking constantly until death eventually comes.

cards.name: Gengar
cards.flavorText: On the night of a full moon, if shadows move on their own and laugh, it must be Gengar's doing.

cards.name: Munna
cards.flavorText: It eats dreams and releases mist. The mist is pink when it's eating a good dream, and black when it's eating a nightmare.

cards.name: Musharna
cards.flavorText: It drowses and dreams all the time. It's best to leave it be if it's just woken up, as it's a terrible grump when freshly roused from sleep.

cards.name: Sinistea
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon is said to have been born when a lonely spirit possessed a cold, leftover cup of tea.

cards.name: Polteageist
cards.flavorText: This species lives in antique teapots. Most pots are forgeries, but on rare occasions, an authentic work is found.

cards.name: Diglett
cards.flavorText: If a Diglett digs through a field, it leaves the soil perfectly tilled and ideal for planting crops.

cards.name: Dugtrio
cards.flavorText: A team of Diglett triplets. It triggers huge earthquakes by burrowing 60 miles underground.

cards.name: Hitmonlee
cards.flavorText: The legs freely contract and stretch. The stretchy legs allow it to hit a distant foe with a rising kick.

cards.name: Hitmonchan
cards.flavorText: Its punches slice the air. However, it seems to need a short break after fighting for three minutes.

cards.name: Rhyhorn
cards.flavorText: It can remember only one thing at a time. Once it starts rushing, it forgets why it started.

cards.name: Rhyhorn
cards.flavorText: Strong, but not too bright, this Pokémon can shatter even a skyscraper with its charging tackles.

cards.name: Rhydon
cards.flavorText: Protected by an armor-like hide, it is capable of living in molten lava of 3,600 degrees Fahrenheit.

cards.name: Rhyperior
cards.flavorText: It relies on its carapace to deflect incoming attacks and throw its enemy off balance. As soon as that happens, it drives its drill into the foe.

cards.name: Sudowoodo
cards.flavorText: If a tree branch shakes when there is no wind, it's a Sudowoodo, not a tree. It hides from the rain.

cards.name: Baltoy
cards.flavorText: It moves while spinning around on its single foot. Some Baltoy have been seen spinning on their heads.

cards.name: Baltoy
cards.flavorText: It moves while spinning around on its single foot. Some Baltoy have been seen spinning on their heads.

cards.name: Claydol
cards.flavorText: This mysterious Pokémon started life as an ancient clay figurine made over 20,000 years ago.

cards.name: Mudbray
cards.flavorText: Loads weighing up to 50 times as much as its own body weight pose no issue for this Pokémon. It's skilled at making use of mud.

cards.name: Mudsdale
cards.flavorText: Mud that hardens around a Mudsdale's legs sets harder than stone. It's so hard that it allows this Pokémon to scrap a truck with a single kick.

cards.name: Silicobra
cards.flavorText: It spews sand from its nostrils. While the enemy is blinded, it burrows into the ground to hide.

cards.name: Silicobra
cards.flavorText: As it digs, it swallows sand and stores it in its neck pouch. The pouch can hold more than 17 pounds of sand.

cards.name: Sandaconda
cards.flavorText: Its unique style of coiling allows it to blast sand out of its sand sac more efficiently.

cards.name: Sandaconda
cards.flavorText: When it contracts its body, over 220 pounds of sand sprays from its nose. If it ever runs out of sand, it becomes disheartened.

cards.name: Clobbopus
cards.flavorText: It's very curious, but its means of investigating things is to try to punch them with its tentacles. The search for food is what brings it onto land.

cards.name: Clobbopus
cards.flavorText: It's very curious, but its means of investigating things is to try to punch them with its tentacles. The search for food is what brings it onto land.

cards.name: Grapploct
cards.flavorText: A body made up of nothing but muscle makes the grappling moves this Pokémon performs with its tentacles tremendously powerful.

cards.name: Stonjourner
cards.flavorText: It stands in grasslands, watching the sun's descent from zenith to horizon. This Pokémon has a talent for delivering dynamic kicks.

cards.name: Galarian Zigzagoon
cards.flavorText: Thought to be the oldest form of Zigzagoon, it moves in zigzags and wreaks havoc upon its surroundings.

cards.name: Galarian Linoone
cards.flavorText: This very aggressive Pokémon will recklessly challenge opponents stronger than itself.

cards.name: Galarian Obstagoon
cards.flavorText: It evolved after experiencing numerous fights. While crossing its arms, it lets out a shout that would make any opponent flinch.

cards.name: Skorupi
cards.flavorText: It attacks using the claws on its tail. Once locked in its grip, its prey is unable to move as this Pokémon's poison seeps in.

cards.name: Drapion
cards.flavorText: It's so vicious that it's called the Sand Demon. Yet when confronted by Hippowdon, Drapion keeps a low profile and will never pick a fight.

cards.name: Croagunk
cards.flavorText: It makes frightening noises with its poison-filled cheek sacs. When opponents flinch, Croagunk hits them with a poison jab.

cards.name: Toxicroak
cards.flavorText: It bounces toward opponents and gouges them with poisonous claws. No more than a scratch is needed to knock out its adversaries.

cards.name: Nickit
cards.flavorText: Aided by the soft pads on its feet, it silently raids the food stores of other Pokémon. It survives off its ill-gotten gains.

cards.name: Thievul
cards.flavorText: It secretly marks potential targets with a scent. By following the scent, it stalks its targets and steals from them when they least expect it.

cards.name: Galarian Meowth
cards.flavorText: Living with a savage, seafaring people has toughened this Pokémon's body so much that parts of it have turned to iron.

cards.name: Galarian Perrserker
cards.flavorText: What appears to be an iron helmet is actually hardened hair. This Pokémon lives for the thrill of battle.

cards.name: Mawile
cards.flavorText: It chomps with its gaping mouth. Its huge jaws are actually steel horns that have been transformed.

cards.name: Ferroseed
cards.flavorText: It defends itself by launching spikes, but its aim isn't very good at first. Only after a lot of practice will it improve.

cards.name: Ferrothorn
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon scrapes its spikes across rocks, and then uses the tips of its feelers to absorb the nutrients it finds within the stone.

cards.name: Galarian Stunfisk
cards.flavorText: Living in mud with a high iron content has given it a strong steel body.

cards.name: Pawniard
cards.flavorText: A pack of these Pokémon forms to serve a Bisharp boss. Each Pawniard trains diligently, dreaming of one day taking the lead.

cards.name: Bisharp
cards.flavorText: Violent conflicts erupt between Bisharp and Fraxure over places where sharpening stones can be found.

cards.name: Corviknight
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon reigns supreme in the skies of the Galar region. The black luster of its steel body could drive terror into the heart of any foe.

cards.name: Cufant
cards.flavorText: If a job requires serious strength, this Pokémon will excel at it. Its copper body tarnishes in the rain, turning a vibrant green color.

cards.name: Copperajah
cards.flavorText: These Pokémon live in herds. Their trunks have incredible grip strength, strong enough to crush giant rocks into powder.

cards.name: Snorlax
cards.flavorText: It is not satisfied unless it eats over 880 pounds of food every day. When it is done eating, it goes promptly to sleep.

cards.name: Hoothoot
cards.flavorText: It begins to hoot at the same time every day. Some Trainers use them in place of clocks.

cards.name: Noctowl
cards.flavorText: When it needs to think, it rotates its head 180 degrees to sharpen its intellectual power.

cards.name: Minccino
cards.flavorText: The way it brushes away grime with its tail can be helpful when cleaning. But its focus on spotlessness can make cleaning more of a hassle.

cards.name: Minccino
cards.flavorText: The way it brushes away grime with its tail can be helpful when cleaning. But its focus on spotlessness can make cleaning more of a hassle.

cards.name: Cinccino
cards.flavorText: Its body secretes oil that this Pokémon spreads over its nest as a coating to protect it from dust. Cinccino won't tolerate even a speck of the stuff.

cards.name: Oranguru
cards.flavorText: It knows the forest inside and out. If it comes across a wounded Pokémon, Oranguru will gather medicinal herbs to treat it.

cards.name: Drampa
cards.flavorText: The mountains it calls home are nearly two miles in height. On rare occasions, it descends to play with the children living in the towns below.

cards.name: Rookidee
cards.flavorText: It will bravely challenge any opponent, no matter how powerful. This Pokémon benefits from every battle—even a defeat increases its strength a bit.

cards.name: Corvisquire
cards.flavorText: Smart enough to use tools in battle, these Pokémon have been seen picking up rocks and flinging them or using ropes to wrap up enemies.

cards.name: Wooloo
cards.flavorText: If its fleece grows too long, Wooloo won't be able to move. Cloth made with the wool of this Pokémon is surprisingly strong.

cards.name: Wooloo
cards.flavorText: Its curly fleece is such an effective cushion that this Pokémon could fall off a cliff and stand right back up at the bottom, unharmed.

cards.name: Dubwool
cards.flavorText: Its majestic horns are meant only to impress the opposite gender. They never see use in battle.

cards.name: Hisuian Voltorb
cards.flavorText: An enigmatic Pokémon that happens to bear a resemblance to a Poké Ball. When excited, it discharges the electric current it has stored in its belly, then lets out a great, uproarious laugh.

cards.name: Hisuian Electrode
cards.flavorText: The tissue on the surface of its body is curiously similar in composition to an Apricorn. When irritated, this Pokémon lets loose an electric current equal to 20 lightning bolts.

cards.name: Scyther
cards.flavorText: The large, wickedly sharp scythes on its forearms are truly fearsome weapons. Prey's attempts to flee are unfailingly thwarted by this Pokémon's nimble motions.

cards.name: Scyther
cards.flavorText: The large, wickedly sharp scythes on its forearms are truly fearsome weapons. Prey's attempts to flee are unfailingly thwarted by this Pokémon's nimble motions.

cards.name: Yanma
cards.flavorText: Its frail wings are so thin that one can see clear through them. However, during flight these wings exhibit the power to churn air with force enough to launch a house skyward.

cards.name: Yanmega
cards.flavorText: This six-legged Pokémon is easily capable of transporting an adult in flight. The wings on its tail help it stay balanced.

cards.name: Heracross
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon has an unparalleled horn. Heracross itself demonstrates tremendous power—it's capable of throwing several people trained in the traditional arts of war at once.

cards.name: Kricketot
cards.flavorText: When its antennae hit each other, it sounds like the music of a xylophone.

cards.name: Kricketune
cards.flavorText: It uses its cutlass-like arms to produce sound, the melody of which varies from individual to individual. It is a worthwhile endeavor to seek out one's favorite tunes.

cards.name: Combee
cards.flavorText: The members of the trio spend all their time together. Each one has a slightly different taste in nectar.

cards.name: Vespiquen
cards.flavorText: It skillfully commands its grubs in battles with its enemies. The grubs are willing to risk their lives to defend Vespiquen.

cards.name: Leafeon
cards.flavorText: Cells similar to those of plants have been found in its fur. Its hard tail can fell a large tree with one stroke, and the tail's sharpness exceeds even that of a sword crafted by a master.

cards.name: Shaymin
cards.flavorText: When the turning of seasons brings the cruel winter to its end and the joyous people give thanks to the heavens, Shaymin appears and covers the withered land with flowers.

cards.name: Petilil
cards.flavorText: The leaves on its head are highly valued for medicinal purposes. Dry the leaves in the sun, boil them, and then drink the bitter decoction for remarkably effective relief from fatigue.

cards.name: Hisuian Lilligant
cards.flavorText: I suspect that its well-developed legs are the result of a life spent on mountains covered in deep snow. The scent it exudes from its flower crown heartens those in proximity.

cards.name: Rowlet
cards.flavorText: Flies noiselessly on delicate wings. It has mastered the art of deftly launching dagger-sharp feathers from those same wings.

cards.name: Dartrix
cards.flavorText: Regularly basks in sunlight to gather power—presumably due to the frigid climate. Nonetheless, the edges of the blade quills set into its wings are keen as ever.

cards.name: Ponyta
cards.flavorText: These Pokémon live in herds out in the grassland. Newborn foals lack their fiery manes, which will develop about an hour after birth.

cards.name: Rapidash
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon can be seen galloping through fields at speeds of up to 150 mph, its fiery mane fluttering in the wind.

cards.name: Cyndaquil
cards.flavorText: Hails from the Johto region. Though usually curled into a ball due to its timid disposition, it harbors tremendous firepower.

cards.name: Quilava
cards.flavorText: This creature's fur is most mysterious—it is wholly impervious to the burning touch of flame. Should Quilava turn its back to you, take heed! Such a posture indicates a forthcoming attack.

cards.name: Radiant Heatran
cards.flavorText: Boiling blood, like magma, circulates through its body. It makes its dwelling place in volcanic caves.

cards.name: Psyduck
cards.flavorText: Suffers perpetual headaches. If the agony grows too great, Psyduck's latent power erupts, contrary to Psyduck's intent. Ergo, I am exploring ways to ease the pain.

cards.name: Golduck
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon lives in gently flowing rivers. It paddles through the water with its long limbs, putting its graceful swimming skills on display.

cards.name: Swinub
cards.flavorText: Swinub excels at sniffing out mushrooms buried beneath grass or snow. Since ancient times, the people of Hisui have often relied upon this skill.

cards.name: Piloswine
cards.flavorText: If it charges at an enemy, the hairs on its back stand up straight. It is very sensitive to sound.

cards.name: Mamoswine
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon can be spotted in wall paintings from as far back as 10,000 years ago. For a while, it was thought to have gone extinct.

cards.name: Mantine
cards.flavorText: This calm and gentle Pokémon swims gracefully through the sea. After building speed, it can leap out of the water. It is often misidentified as a bird Pokémon due to this behavior.

cards.name: Barboach
cards.flavorText: Makes its home in swamps with murky water. The poor visibility hides this Pokémon from predators, and the slime on its body makes grasping it difficult.

cards.name: Whiscash
cards.flavorText: It makes its nest at the bottom of swamps. It will eat anything—if it is alive, Whiscash will eat it.

cards.name: Regice
cards.flavorText: With cold air that can reach temperatures as low as −328 degrees Fahrenheit, Regice instantly freezes any creature that approaches it.

cards.name: Glaceon
cards.flavorText: Glaceon is able to lower its body temperature very quickly. It freezes the atmosphere, creating diamond dust that glitters like gems while it flutters and dances around.

cards.name: Oshawott
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon from the Unova region uses the shell on its belly as a weapon to cut down its foes. Thus, I've conferred upon this shell the name "scalchop.".

cards.name: Dewott
cards.flavorText: Its exquisite double-scalchop technique is likely the result of daily training, and it can send even masters of the blade fleeing in defeat.

cards.name: Hisuian Basculin
cards.flavorText: Though it differs from other Basculin in several respects, including demeanor—this one is gentle—I have categorized it as a regional form given the vast array of shared qualities.

cards.name: Hisuian Basculegion
cards.flavorText: Clads itself in the souls of comrades that perished before fulfilling their goals of journeying upstream. No other species throughout all Hisui's rivers is Basculegion's equal.

cards.name: Keldeo
cards.flavorText: When it is resolute, its body fills with power and it becomes swifter. Its jumps are then too fast to follow.

cards.name: Radiant Greninja
cards.flavorText: It appears and vanishes with a ninja's grace. It toys with its enemies using swift movements, while slicing them with throwing stars of sharpest water.

cards.name: Bergmite
cards.flavorText: Lives on mountains blanketed in perennial snow. It freezes water vapor in the air to make the ice helmet that it dons for defense.

cards.name: Hisuian Avalugg
cards.flavorText: The armor of ice covering its lower jaw puts steel to shame and can shatter rocks with ease. This Pokémon barrels along steep mountain paths, cleaving through the deep snow.

cards.name: Regieleki
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon is a cluster of electrical energy. It's said that removing the rings on Regieleki's body will unleash the Pokémon's latent power.

cards.name: Hisuian Typhlosion
cards.flavorText: Said to purify lost, forsaken souls with its flames and guide them to the afterlife. I believe its form has been influenced by the energy of the sacred mountain towering at Hisui's center.

cards.name: Togepi
cards.flavorText: This ovate creature is frequently mistaken for a moving egg when encountered out in the fields or in the mountains. Its guileless smile soothes the soul.

cards.name: Togetic
cards.flavorText: They say that it will appear before kindhearted, caring people and shower them with happiness.

cards.name: Togekiss
cards.flavorText: These Pokémon are never seen anywhere near conflict or turmoil. In recent times, they've hardly been seen at all.

cards.name: Misdreavus
cards.flavorText: It conceals itself in darkness, sending chills up travelers' spines with its childlike weeping. As it observes the frightened travelers with glee, the red orbs upon its chest let off an eerie light.

cards.name: Mismagius
cards.flavorText: Its muttered curses can cause awful headaches or terrifying visions that torment others.

cards.name: Ralts
cards.flavorText: Tends to prefer people with a chipper disposition to those who are gloomy, but it has shown no discrimination with regard to age or gender. Needs more research.

cards.name: Kirlia
cards.flavorText: If its Trainer becomes happy, it overflows with energy, dancing joyously while spinning about.

cards.name: Gallade
cards.flavorText: True to its honorable-warrior image, it uses the blades on its elbows only in defense of something or someone.

cards.name: Drifloon
cards.flavorText: Said to lure away young children and carry them off to the afterlife. Some whisper that Drifloon are formed of reincarnated human souls, but these rumors are as yet unconfirmed.

cards.name: Drifblim
cards.flavorText: Some say this Pokémon is a collection of souls burdened with regrets, silently drifting through the dusk.

cards.name: Uxie
cards.flavorText: It is said that its emergence gave humans the intelligence to improve their quality of life.

cards.name: Mesprit
cards.flavorText: It sleeps at the bottom of a lake. Its spirit is said to leave its body to fly on the lake's surface.

cards.name: Azelf
cards.flavorText: It is thought that Uxie, Mesprit, and Azelf all came from the same egg.

cards.name: Diancie
cards.flavorText: It can instantly create many diamonds by compressing the carbon in the air between its hands.

cards.name: Wyrdeer
cards.flavorText: The black orbs shine with an uncanny light when the Pokémon is erecting invisible barriers. The fur shed from its beard retains heat well and is a highly useful material for winter clothing.

cards.name: Hisuian Growlithe
cards.flavorText: They patrol their territory in pairs. I believe the igneous rock components in the fur of this species are the result of volcanic activity in its habitat.

cards.name: Hisuian Arcanine
cards.flavorText: Snaps at its foes with fangs cloaked in blazing flame. Despite its bulk, it deftly feints every which way, leading opponents on a deceptively merry chase as it all but dances around them.

cards.name: Sudowoodo
cards.flavorText: Though it pretends to be a tree, it fails to fool even children. To the touch, its body feels more like rock than tree bark. Sudowoodo's extreme aversion to water merits special note.

cards.name: Regirock
cards.flavorText: Every bit of Regirock's body is made of stone. As parts of its body erode, this Pokémon sticks rocks to itself to repair what's been lost.

cards.name: Cranidos
cards.flavorText: Its hard skull is its distinguishing feature. It snapped trees by headbutting them, and then it fed on their ripe berries.

cards.name: Rampardos
cards.flavorText: This ancient Pokémon used headbutts skillfully. Its brain was really small, so some theories suggest that its stupidity led to its extinction.

cards.name: Hippopotas
cards.flavorText: Though large and languid, Hippopotas is difficult to detect due to its tendency to burrow into and lurk beneath the soil. When agitated or excited, it expels sand from its nostrils.

cards.name: Hippowdon
cards.flavorText: Stones can get stuck in the ports on their bodies. Dwebble help dislodge such stones, so Hippowdon look after these Pokémon.

cards.name: Radiant Hawlucha
cards.flavorText: It drives its opponents to exhaustion with its agile maneuvers, then ends the fight with a flashy finishing move.

cards.name: Hisuian Decidueye
cards.flavorText: The air stored inside the rachises of Decidueye's feathers insulates the Pokémon against Hisui's extreme cold. This is firm proof that evolution can be influenced by environment.

cards.name: Kleavor
cards.flavorText: A violent creature that fells towering trees with its crude axes and shields itself with hard stone. If one should chance upon this Pokémon in the wilds, one's only recourse is to flee.

cards.name: Kleavor
cards.flavorText: A violent creature that fells towering trees with its crude axes and shields itself with hard stone. If one should chance upon this Pokémon in the wilds, one's only recourse is to flee.

cards.name: Hisuian Qwilfish
cards.flavorText: Fishers detest this troublesome Pokémon because it sprays poison from its spines, getting it everywhere. A different form of Qwilfish lives in other regions.

cards.name: Hisuian Qwilfish
cards.flavorText: Fishers detest this troublesome Pokémon because it sprays poison from its spines, getting it everywhere. A different form of Qwilfish lives in other regions.

cards.name: Hisuian Overqwil
cards.flavorText: Its lancelike spikes and savage temperament have earned it the nickname "sea fiend." It slurps up poison to nourish itself.

cards.name: Hisuian Overqwil
cards.flavorText: Its lancelike spikes and savage temperament have earned it the nickname "sea fiend." It slurps up poison to nourish itself.

cards.name: Hisuian Sneasel
cards.flavorText: Its sturdy, curved claws are ideal for traversing precipitous cliffs. From the tips of these claws drips a venom that infiltrates the nerves of any prey caught in Sneasel's grasp.

cards.name: Hisuian Sneasler
cards.flavorText: Because of Sneasler's virulent poison and daunting physical prowess, no other species could hope to best it on the frozen highlands. Preferring solitude, this species does not form packs.

cards.name: Poochyena
cards.flavorText: It has a very tenacious nature. Its acute sense of smell lets it chase a chosen prey without ever losing track.

cards.name: Mightyena
cards.flavorText: It chases down prey in a pack of around ten. They defeat foes with perfectly coordinated teamwork.

cards.name: Absol
cards.flavorText: Swift as the wind, Absol races through fields and mountains. Its curved, bow-like horn is acutely sensitive to the warning signs of natural disasters.

cards.name: Hisuian Samurott
cards.flavorText: Hard of heart and deft of blade, this rare form of Samurott is a product of the Pokémon's evolution in the region of Hisui. Its turbulent blows crash into foes like ceaseless pounding waves.

cards.name: Nickit
cards.flavorText: Aided by the soft pads on its feet, it silently raids the food stores of other Pokémon. It survives off its ill-gotten gains.

cards.name: Thievul
cards.flavorText: It secretly marks potential targets with a scent. By following the scent, it stalks its targets and steals from them when they least expect it.

cards.name: Magnemite
cards.flavorText: A bizarre Pokémon with but a single eye embedded in an iron sphere. I suspect this creature levitates due to the magnetism it emits from its arms, which resemble horseshoe-shaped magnets.

cards.name: Magneton
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon is three Magnemite that have linked together. Magneton sends out powerful radio waves to study its surroundings.

cards.name: Magnezone
cards.flavorText: Some say that Magnezone receives signals from space via the antenna on its head and that it's being controlled by some mysterious being.

cards.name: Registeel
cards.flavorText: Registeel's body is made of a strange material that is flexible enough to stretch and shrink but also more durable than any metal.

cards.name: Shieldon
cards.flavorText: Although its fossils can be found in layers of primeval rock, nothing but its face has ever been discovered.

cards.name: Bastiodon
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon is from roughly 100 million years ago. Its terrifyingly tough face is harder than steel.

cards.name: Bronzor
cards.flavorText: Floats using a mysterious energy. The pattern engraved upon its back is held as sacred and can sometimes be found in imagery from ancient cemeteries and other such timeworn places.

cards.name: Bronzong
cards.flavorText: Some believe it to be a deity that summons rain clouds. When angered, it lets out a warning cry that rings out like the tolling of a bell.

cards.name: Pawniard
cards.flavorText: It uses river stones to maintain the cutting edges of the blades covering its body. These sharpened blades allow it to bring down opponents.

cards.name: Bisharp
cards.flavorText: It's accompanied by a large retinue of Pawniard. Bisharp keeps a keen eye on its minions, ensuring none of them even think of double-crossing it.

cards.name: Regidrago
cards.flavorText: An academic theory proposes that Regidrago's arms were once the head of an ancient dragon Pokémon. The theory remains unproven.

cards.name: Eevee
cards.flavorText: It has the ability to alter the composition of its body to suit its surrounding environment.

cards.name: Hoothoot
cards.flavorText: It always stands on one foot. It changes feet so fast, the movement can rarely be seen.

cards.name: Noctowl
cards.flavorText: Its eyes are specially developed to enable it to see clearly even in murky darkness and minimal light.

cards.name: Teddiursa
cards.flavorText: It licks its paws because of the sweet honey that has soaked into them. It is cunning, stealing into the nests of Combee and taking for itself the honey that the Combee have amassed.

cards.name: Ursaring
cards.flavorText: When the cold season arrives in Hisui, this Pokémon will wander fields and mountains alike in search of its favorite berries. Ursaring's hunger during this time makes it a ferocious danger.

cards.name: Ursaluna
cards.flavorText: I believe it was Hisui's swampy terrain that gave Ursaluna its burly physique and newfound capacity to manipulate peat at will.

cards.name: Stantler
cards.flavorText: Its strangely shaped antlers have the power to bewitch those who see them. Medicine made by grinding up the black orbs from fallen antlers is an effective treatment for insomnia.

cards.name: Miltank
cards.flavorText: Miltank produces highly nutritious milk, so it's been supporting the lives of people and other Pokémon since ancient times.

cards.name: Glameow
cards.flavorText: Bewitches humans with its helical tail and piercing gaze. Its hidden claws are quite sharp as well, making this Pokémon an exceedingly tricky opponent if antagonized.

cards.name: Purugly
cards.flavorText: To make itself appear intimidatingly beefy, it tightly cinches its waist with its twin tails.

cards.name: Chatot
cards.flavorText: A versatile performer skilled in the imitation of human speech. It is said that older, more experienced Chatot can even understand the meaning of the words they mimic.

cards.name: Regigigas
cards.flavorText: There is an enduring legend that states this Pokémon towed continents with ropes.

cards.name: Rufflet
cards.flavorText: Its chick-like looks belie its hotheadedness. It challenges its parents at every opportunity, desperate to prove its strength.

cards.name: Hisuian Braviary
cards.flavorText: Screaming a bloodcurdling battle cry, this huge and ferocious bird Pokémon goes out on the hunt. It blasts lakes with shock waves, then scoops up any prey that float to the water's surface.

cards.name: Abomasnow
cards.flavorText: The Pokémon is known to bring blizzards. A shake of its massive body is enough to cause whiteout conditions.

cards.name: Flapple
cards.flavorText: It ate a sour apple, and that induced its evolution. In its cheeks, it stores an acid capable of causing chemical burns.

cards.name: Kingdra
cards.flavorText: It stores energy by sleeping at underwater depths at which no other life forms can survive.

cards.name: Frosmoth
cards.flavorText: It shows no mercy to any who desecrate fields and mountains. It will fly around on its icy wings, causing a blizzard to chase offenders away.

cards.name: Gardevoir
cards.flavorText: To protect its Trainer, it will expend all its psychic power to create a small black hole.

cards.name: Wyrdeer
cards.flavorText: The black orbs shine with an uncanny light when the Pokémon is erecting invisible barriers. The fur shed from its beard retains heat well and is a highly useful material for winter clothing.

cards.name: Falinks
cards.flavorText: The six of them work together as one Pokémon. Teamwork is also their battle strategy, and they constantly change their formation as they fight.

cards.name: Kleavor
cards.flavorText: A violent creature that fells towering trees with its crude axes and shields itself with hard stone. If one should chance upon this Pokémon in the wilds, one's only recourse is to flee.

cards.name: Mightyena
cards.flavorText: It chases down prey in a pack of around ten. They defeat foes with perfectly coordinated teamwork.

cards.name: Galarian Obstagoon
cards.flavorText: It evolved after experiencing numerous fights. While crossing its arms, it lets out a shout that would make any opponent flinch.

cards.name: Bronzong
cards.flavorText: Many scientists suspect that this Pokémon originated outside the Galar region, based on the patterns on its body.

cards.name: Hoothoot
cards.flavorText: It always stands on one foot. It changes feet so fast, the movement can rarely be seen.

cards.name: Oddish
cards.flavorText: If exposed to moonlight, it starts to move. It roams far and wide at night to scatter its seeds.

cards.name: Gloom
cards.flavorText: Its pistils exude an incredibly foul odor. The horrid stench can cause fainting at a distance of 1.25 miles.

cards.name: Vileplume
cards.flavorText: It has the world's largest petals. With every step, the petals shake out heavy clouds of toxic pollen.

cards.name: Paras
cards.flavorText: The mushrooms, known as tochukaso, are controlling the bug. Even if the bug bugs the mushrooms, they tell it to bug off.

cards.name: Parasect
cards.flavorText: The bug is mostly dead, with the mushroom on its back having become the main body. If the mushroom comes off, the bug stops moving.

cards.name: Wurmple
cards.flavorText: It lives among the tall grass and in forests. It repels attacks by raising up the spikes on its rear.

cards.name: Silcoon
cards.flavorText: It drinks dew that collects on its silk and waits for evolution. Its hard cocoon repels attacks.

cards.name: Beautifly
cards.flavorText: It has an aggressive nature. It stabs prey with its long, narrow mouth to drain the prey's fluids.

cards.name: Cascoon
cards.flavorText: It never forgets any attack it endured while in the cocoon. After evolution, it seeks payback.

cards.name: Dustox
cards.flavorText: Tends to be drawn to bonfires on dark nights. Difficult to chase away from settlements because of the way it scatters highly toxic scales.

cards.name: Seedot
cards.flavorText: If it remains still, it looks just like a real nut. It delights in surprising foraging Pokémon.

cards.name: Nuzleaf
cards.flavorText: It lives deep in forests. With the leaf on its head, it makes a flute whose song makes listeners uneasy.

cards.name: Shiftry
cards.flavorText: A Pokémon that was feared as a forest guardian. It can read the foe's mind and take preemptive action.

cards.name: Roselia
cards.flavorText: Its flowers give off a relaxing fragrance. The stronger its aroma, the healthier the Roselia is.

cards.name: Roserade
cards.flavorText: After captivating opponents with its sweet scent, it lashes them with its thorny whips.

cards.name: Phantump
cards.flavorText: After a lost child perished in the forest, their spirit possessed a tree stump, causing the spirit's rebirth as this Pokémon.

cards.name: Trevenant
cards.flavorText: People fear it due to a belief that it devours any who try to cut down trees in its forest, but to the Pokémon it shares its woods with, it's kind.

cards.name: Blipbug
cards.flavorText: A constant collector of information, this Pokémon is very smart. Very strong is what it isn't.

cards.name: Dottler
cards.flavorText: It barely moves, but it's still alive. Hiding in its shell without food or water seems to have awakened its psychic powers.

cards.name: Orbeetle
cards.flavorText: It's famous for its high level of intelligence, and the large size of its brain is proof that it also possesses immense psychic power.

cards.name: Slugma
cards.flavorText: Its body is made of magma. If it doesn't keep moving, its body will cool and harden.

cards.name: Magcargo
cards.flavorText: Its body is as hot as lava and is always billowing. Flames will occasionally burst from its shell.

cards.name: Torkoal
cards.flavorText: It burns coal inside its shell for energy. It blows out black soot if it is endangered.

cards.name: Litwick
cards.flavorText: The flame on its head keeps its body slightly warm. This Pokémon takes lost children by the hand to guide them to the spirit world.

cards.name: Lampent
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon appears just before someone passes away, so it's feared as an emissary of death.

cards.name: Chandelure
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon haunts dilapidated mansions. It sways its arms to hypnotize opponents with the ominous dancing of its flames.

cards.name: Litleo
cards.flavorText: This hot-blooded Pokémon is filled with curiosity. When it gets angry or starts fighting, its short mane gets hot.

cards.name: Pyroar
cards.flavorText: The temperature of its breath is over 10,000 degrees Fahrenheit, but Pyroar doesn't use it on its prey. This Pokémon prefers to eat raw meat.

cards.name: Poliwag
cards.flavorText: For Poliwag, swimming is easier than walking. The swirl pattern on its belly is actually part of the Pokémon's innards showing through the skin.

cards.name: Poliwhirl
cards.flavorText: Staring at the swirl on its belly causes drowsiness. This trait of Poliwhirl's has been used in place of lullabies to get children to go to sleep.

cards.name: Politoed
cards.flavorText: At nightfall, these Pokémon appear on the shores of lakes. They announce their territorial claims by letting out cries that sound like shouting.

cards.name: Seel
cards.flavorText: Thanks to its thick fat, cold seas don't bother it at all, but it gets tired pretty easily in warm waters.

cards.name: Dewgong
cards.flavorText: It sunbathes on the beach after meals. The rise in its body temperature helps its digestion.

cards.name: Horsea
cards.flavorText: Horsea makes its home in oceans with gentle currents. If this Pokémon is under attack, it spits out pitch-black ink and escapes.

cards.name: Seadra
cards.flavorText: It's the males that raise the offspring. While Seadra are raising young, the spines on their backs secrete thicker and stronger poison.

cards.name: Kingdra
cards.flavorText: With the arrival of a storm at sea, this Pokémon will show itself on the surface. When a Kingdra and a Dragonite meet, a fierce battle ensues.

cards.name: Luvdisc
cards.flavorText: Luvdisc makes its home in coral reefs in warm seas. It especially likes sleeping in the space between Corsola's branches.

cards.name: Shellos
cards.flavorText: There's speculation that its appearance is determined by what it eats, but the truth remains elusive.

cards.name: Finneon
cards.flavorText: It lures in prey with its shining tail fins. It stays near the surface during the day and moves to the depths when night falls.

cards.name: Lumineon
cards.flavorText: They traverse the deep waters as if crawling over the seafloor. The fantastic lights of its fins shine like stars in the night sky.

cards.name: Snover
cards.flavorText: One is likely to encounter this Pokémon while out in the snow. There are stories of Snover appearing in human settlements but doing no harm—rather, they bond with the children.

cards.name: Abomasnow
cards.flavorText: If it sees any packs of Darumaka going after Snover, it chases them off, swinging its sizable arms like hammers.

cards.name: Hisuian Basculin
cards.flavorText: Though it differs from other Basculin in several respects, including demeanor—this one is gentle—I have categorized it as a regional form given the vast array of shared qualities.

cards.name: Hisuian Basculegion
cards.flavorText: Clads itself in the souls of comrades that perished before fulfilling their goals of journeying upstream. No other species throughout all Hisui's rivers is Basculegion's equal.

cards.name: Ducklett
cards.flavorText: They are better at swimming than flying, and they happily eat their favorite food, peat moss, as they dive underwater.

cards.name: Swanna
cards.flavorText: Swanna start to dance at dusk. The one dancing in the middle is the leader of the flock.

cards.name: Cramorant
cards.flavorText: It's so strong that it can knock out some opponents in a single hit, but it also may forget what it's battling midfight.

cards.name: Glastrier
cards.flavorText: Glastrier emits intense cold from its hooves. It's also a belligerent Pokémon—anything it wants, it takes by force.

cards.name: Pikachu
cards.flavorText: Pikachu that can generate powerful electricity have cheek sacs that are extra soft and super stretchy.

cards.name: Raichu
cards.flavorText: Its long tail serves as a ground to protect itself from its own high-voltage power.

cards.name: Electrike
cards.flavorText: It stores static electricity in its fur for discharging. It gives off sparks if a storm approaches.

cards.name: Manectric
cards.flavorText: It stimulates its own muscles with electricity, so it can move quickly. It eases its soreness with electricity, too, so it can recover quickly as well.

cards.name: Tynamo
cards.flavorText: One alone can emit only a trickle of electricity, so a group of them gathers to unleash a powerful electric shock.

cards.name: Eelektrik
cards.flavorText: These Pokémon have a big appetite. When they spot their prey, they attack it and paralyze it with electricity.

cards.name: Eelektross
cards.flavorText: They crawl out of the ocean using their arms. They will attack prey on shore and immediately drag it into the ocean.

cards.name: Clefairy
cards.flavorText: It can be found in quiet mountain areas on a full moon's night. Its dancing and its tiny, faintly glowing wings confer upon it a lovely fairylike quality.

cards.name: Clefable
cards.flavorText: A timid fairy Pokémon that is rarely seen, it will run and hide the moment it senses people.

cards.name: Gastly
cards.flavorText: Born from gases, anyone would faint if engulfed by its gaseous body, which contains poison.

cards.name: Haunter
cards.flavorText: This frightful, malevolent spirit can glide through walls, appearing wherever it likes. According to rumor, victims of a Haunter's lick will wither to death day by day.

cards.name: Gengar
cards.flavorText: On the night of a full moon, if shadows move on their own and laugh, it must be Gengar's doing.

cards.name: Mr. Mime
cards.flavorText: The behavior of this clown-like Pokémon reminds one of pantomime. It creates invisible walls using a force emitted from its fingertips.

cards.name: Jynx
cards.flavorText: Its strange cries sound like human language. There are some musicians who compose songs for Jynx to sing.

cards.name: Radiant Gardevoir
cards.flavorText: It has the power to predict the future. Its power peaks when it is protecting its Trainer.

cards.name: Sableye
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon is feared. When its gemstone eyes begin to glow with a sinister shine, it's believed that Sableye will steal people's spirits away.

cards.name: Mawile
cards.flavorText: It uses its docile-looking face to lull foes into complacency, then bites with its huge, relentless jaws.

cards.name: Shuppet
cards.flavorText: There's a proverb that says, "Shun the house where Shuppet gather in the growing dusk."

cards.name: Banette
cards.flavorText: Resentment at being cast off made it spring into being. Some say that treating it well will satisfy it, and it will once more become a stuffed toy.

cards.name: Cresselia
cards.flavorText: Those who sleep holding Cresselia's feather are assured of joyful dreams. It is said to represent the crescent moon.

cards.name: Hisuian Zorua
cards.flavorText: A once-departed soul, returned to life in Hisui. Derives power from resentment, which rises as energy atop its head and takes on the forms of foes. In this way, Zorua vents lingering malice.

cards.name: Hisuian Zoroark
cards.flavorText: With its disheveled white fur, it looks like an embodiment of death. Heedless of its own safety, Zoroark attacks its nemeses with a bitter energy so intense, it lacerates Zoroark's own body.

cards.name: Inkay
cards.flavorText: It spins while making its luminescent spots flash. These spots allow it to communicate with others by using different patterns of light.

cards.name: Malamar
cards.flavorText: Gazing at its luminescent spots will quickly induce a hypnotic state, putting the observer under Malamar's control.

cards.name: Comfey
cards.flavorText: Comfey picks flowers with its vine and decorates itself with them. For some reason, flowers won't wither once they're attached to a Comfey.

cards.name: Mimikyu
cards.flavorText: It wears a rag fashioned into a Pikachu costume in an effort to look less scary. Unfortunately, the costume only makes it creepier.

cards.name: Spectrier
cards.flavorText: It probes its surroundings with all its senses save one—it doesn't use its sense of sight. Spectrier's kicks are said to separate soul from body.

cards.name: Hisuian Growlithe
cards.flavorText: They patrol their territory in pairs. I believe the igneous rock components in the fur of this species are the result of volcanic activity in its habitat.

cards.name: Hisuian Arcanine
cards.flavorText: Snaps at its foes with fangs cloaked in blazing flame. Despite its bulk, it deftly feints every which way, leading opponents on a deceptively merry chase as it all but dances around them.

cards.name: Poliwrath
cards.flavorText: Its body is solid muscle. When swimming through cold seas, Poliwrath uses its impressive arms to smash through drift ice and plow forward.

cards.name: Machop
cards.flavorText: Its whole body is composed of muscles. Even though it's the size of a human child, it can hurl 100 grown-ups.

cards.name: Machoke
cards.flavorText: A sturdy creature boasting a robust physique and boundless stamina. Loves training above all else and voluntarily assists with tasks such as construction and clearing land.

cards.name: Machamp
cards.flavorText: It quickly swings its four arms to rock its opponents with ceaseless punches and chops from all angles.

cards.name: Rhyhorn
cards.flavorText: Strong, but not too bright, this Pokémon can shatter even a skyscraper with its charging tackles.

cards.name: Rhydon
cards.flavorText: It begins walking on its hind legs after evolution. It can punch holes through boulders with its horn.

cards.name: Rhyperior
cards.flavorText: It can load up to three projectiles per arm into the holes in its hands. What launches out of those holes could be either rocks or Roggenrola.

cards.name: Sudowoodo
cards.flavorText: Though it pretends to be a tree, it fails to fool even children. To the touch, its body feels more like rock than tree bark. Sudowoodo's extreme aversion to water merits special note.

cards.name: Gligar
cards.flavorText: It flies straight at its target's face, then clamps down on the startled victim to inject poison.

cards.name: Gliscor
cards.flavorText: Its flight is soundless. It uses its lengthy tail to carry off its prey... Then its elongated fangs do the rest.

cards.name: Makuhita
cards.flavorText: There's a rumor of a traditional recipe for stew that Trainers can use to raise strong Makuhita.

cards.name: Hariyama
cards.flavorText: Hariyama that are big and fat aren't necessarily strong. There are some small ones that move nimbly and use moves skillfully.

cards.name: Meditite
cards.flavorText: It eats just one berry a day. By enduring hunger, its spirit is tempered and made sharper.

cards.name: Medicham
cards.flavorText: Through yoga training, it gained the psychic power to predict its foe's next move.

cards.name: Relicanth
cards.flavorText: Rock-hard scales and oil-filled swim bladders allow this Pokémon to survive the intense water pressure of the deep sea.

cards.name: Gastrodon
cards.flavorText: Its search for food sometimes leads it onto land, where it leaves behind a sticky trail of slime as it passes through.

cards.name: Mienfoo
cards.flavorText: In one minute, a well-trained Mienfoo can chop with its arms more than 100 times.

cards.name: Mienshao
cards.flavorText: When Mienshao comes across a truly challenging opponent, it will lighten itself by biting off the fur on its arms.

cards.name: Landorus
cards.flavorText: From the forces of lightning and wind, it creates energy to give nutrients to the soil and make the land abundant.

cards.name: Binacle
cards.flavorText: After two Binacle find a suitably sized rock, they adhere themselves to it and live together. They cooperate to gather food during high tide.

cards.name: Barbaracle
cards.flavorText: Seven Binacle come together to form one Barbaracle. The Binacle that serves as the head gives orders to those serving as the limbs.

cards.name: Carbink
cards.flavorText: When beset by attackers, Carbink wipes them all out by firing high-energy beams from the gems embedded in its body.

cards.name: Rockruff
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon can bond very strongly with its Trainer, but it also has a habit of biting. Raising a Rockruff for a long time can be challenging.

cards.name: Falinks
cards.flavorText: Five of them are troopers, and one is the brass. The brass's orders are absolute.

cards.name: Stonjourner
cards.flavorText: It stands in grasslands, watching the sun's descent from zenith to horizon. This Pokémon has a talent for delivering dynamic kicks.

cards.name: Spinarak
cards.flavorText: Although the poison from its fangs isn't that strong, it's potent enough to weaken prey that gets caught in its web.

cards.name: Ariados
cards.flavorText: It spews threads from its mouth to catch its prey. When night falls, it leaves its web to go hunt aggressively.

cards.name: Murkrow
cards.flavorText: It searches for shiny things for its boss. Murkrow's presence is said to be unlucky, so many people detest it.

cards.name: Honchkrow
cards.flavorText: Its goons take care of most of the fighting for it. The only time it dirties its own hands is in delivering a final blow to finish off an opponent.

cards.name: Seviper
cards.flavorText: Constant polishing makes the edge of the blade on its tail extremely sharp. It's Zangoose's archrival.

cards.name: Spiritomb
cards.flavorText: Exactly 108 spirits gathered to become this Pokémon. Apparently there are some ill-natured spirits in the mix.

cards.name: Darkrai
cards.flavorText: On a moonless night, a strange incident occurred in which every one of a village's inhabitants suffered nightmares. The villagers attested that Darkrai appeared before them in these nightmares.

cards.name: Inkay
cards.flavorText: It spins while making its luminescent spots flash. These spots allow it to communicate with others by using different patterns of light.

cards.name: Hoopa
cards.flavorText: It gathers things it likes and passes them through its loop to teleport them to a secret place.

cards.name: Radiant Hisuian Sneasler
cards.flavorText: Because of Sneasler's virulent poison and daunting physical prowess, no other species could hope to best it on the frozen highlands. Preferring solitude, this species does not form packs.

cards.name: Radiant Steelix
cards.flavorText: It is said that if an Onix lives for over 100 years, its composition changes to become diamond-like.

cards.name: Bronzor
cards.flavorText: It appears in ancient ruins. The pattern on its body doesn't come from any culture in the Galar region, so it remains shrouded in mystery.

cards.name: Bronzong
cards.flavorText: Some believe that its bell-like cry opens holes to another world. It has been revered as a deity since ancient times.

cards.name: Galarian Stunfisk
cards.flavorText: Living in mud with a high iron content has given it a strong steel body.

cards.name: Magearna
cards.flavorText: Built roughly 500 years ago by a scientist, the part called the Soul-Heart is the actual life-form.

cards.name: Goomy
cards.flavorText: Goomy hides away in the shade of trees, where it's nice and humid. If the slime coating its body dries out, the Pokémon instantly becomes lethargic.

cards.name: Hisuian Sliggoo
cards.flavorText: A creature given to melancholy. I suspect its metallic shell developed as a result of the mucus on its skin reacting with the iron in Hisui's water.

cards.name: Hisuian Goodra
cards.flavorText: Able to freely control the hardness of its metallic shell. It loathes solitude and is extremely clingy—it will fume and run riot if those dearest to it ever leave its side.

cards.name: Lickitung
cards.flavorText: If this Pokémon's sticky saliva gets on you and you don't clean it off, an intense itch will set in. The itch won't go away, either.

cards.name: Lickilicky
cards.flavorText: Lickilicky's strange tongue can stretch to many times the length of its body. No one has figured out how Lickilicky's tongue can stretch so far.

cards.name: Porygon
cards.flavorText: State-of-the-art technology was used to create Porygon. It was the first artificial Pokémon to be created via computer programming.

cards.name: Porygon2
cards.flavorText: This is a Porygon that was updated with special data. Porygon2 develops itself by learning about many different subjects all on its own.

cards.name: Porygon-Z
cards.flavorText: Porygon-Z had a program installed to allow it to move between dimensions, but the program also caused instability in Porygon-Z's behavior.

cards.name: Snorlax
cards.flavorText: It is not satisfied unless it eats over 880 pounds of food every day. When it is done eating, it goes promptly to sleep.

cards.name: Aipom
cards.flavorText: This treetop dweller possesses a tail as dexterous as a hand. Ancient writings describe this Pokémon as a one-armed oddity.

cards.name: Ambipom
cards.flavorText: It uses its tails for everything. If it wraps both of its tails around you and gives you a squeeze, that's proof it really likes you.

cards.name: Bouffalant
cards.flavorText: These Pokémon can crush a car with no more than a headbutt. Bouffalant with more hair on their heads hold higher positions within the herd.

cards.name: Komala
cards.flavorText: It remains asleep from birth to death as a result of the sedative properties of the leaves that form its diet.

cards.name: Skwovet
cards.flavorText: Found throughout the Galar region, this Pokémon becomes uneasy if its cheeks are ever completely empty of berries.

cards.name: Greedent
cards.flavorText: It stashes berries in its tail—so many berries that they fall out constantly. But this Pokémon is a bit slow-witted, so it doesn't notice the loss.

cards.name: Parasect
cards.flavorText: Mushroom-lacking specimens of this Pokémon lie unmoving in the forest, lending credence to the hypothesis that the large mushroom is in control of Parasect's actions.

cards.name: Roserade
cards.flavorText: After captivating opponents with its sweet scent, it lashes them with its thorny whips.

cards.name: Charizard
cards.flavorText: It spits fire that is hot enough to melt boulders. It may cause forest fires by blowing flames.

cards.name: Chandelure
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon haunts dilapidated mansions. It sways its arms to hypnotize opponents with the ominous dancing of its flames.

cards.name: Pikachu
cards.flavorText: Possesses cheek sacs in which it stores electricity. This clever forest-dweller roasts tough berries with an electric shock before consuming them.

cards.name: Gengar
cards.flavorText: Possesses potential victims' shadows in an effort to steal away the victims' lives. If your shadow begins to laugh, you must take hold of a protective charm posthaste!

cards.name: Banette
cards.flavorText: Resentment at being cast off made it spring into being. Some say that treating it well will satisfy it, and it will once more become a stuffed toy.

cards.name: Hisuian Arcanine
cards.flavorText: Snaps at its foes with fangs cloaked in blazing flame. Despite its bulk, it deftly feints every which way, leading opponents on a deceptively merry chase as it all but dances around them.

cards.name: Spiritomb
cards.flavorText: It lays curses by thinking wicked thoughts. Writings tell that this Pokémon was born out of the assembly of five score and eight malevolent spirits.

cards.name: Snorlax
cards.flavorText: This glutton appears in villages without warning and devours the entirety of their rice granaries—such occurrences have long been counted among the gravest of disasters.

cards.name: Castform
cards.flavorText: Its form changes depending on the weather. The rougher conditions get, the rougher Castform's disposition!

cards.name: Boss's Orders
cards.flavorText: Lysandre

cards.name: Venonat
cards.flavorText: Lives in the shadows of tall trees where it eats bugs. It is attracted by light at night.

cards.name: Venomoth
cards.flavorText: The wings are covered with dustlike scales. Every time it flaps its wings, it looses highly toxic dust.

cards.name: Spinarak
cards.flavorText: Although the poison from its fangs isn't that strong, it's potent enough to weaken prey that gets caught in its web.

cards.name: Ariados
cards.flavorText: It spews threads from its mouth to catch its prey. When night falls, it leaves its web to go hunt aggressively.

cards.name: Sunkern
cards.flavorText: It lives by drinking only dewdrops from under the leaves of plants. It is said that it eats nothing else.

cards.name: Sunflora
cards.flavorText: It gets energy from warm sunlight and is known for its habit of moving in pursuit of it.

cards.name: Petilil
cards.flavorText: The leaves on its head are highly valued for medicinal purposes. Dry the leaves in the sun, boil them, and then drink the bitter decoction for remarkably effective relief from fatigue.

cards.name: Hisuian Lilligant
cards.flavorText: I suspect that its well-developed legs are the result of a life spent on mountains covered in deep snow. The scent it exudes from its flower crown heartens those in proximity.

cards.name: Foongus
cards.flavorText: No one knows what the Poké Ball–like pattern on Foongus means or why Foongus has it.

cards.name: Amoonguss
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon puffs poisonous spores at its foes. If the spores aren't washed off quickly, they'll grow into mushrooms wherever they land.

cards.name: Durant
cards.flavorText: They lay their eggs deep inside their nests. When attacked by Heatmor, they retaliate using their massive mandibles.

cards.name: Virizion
cards.flavorText: A legend tells of this Pokémon working together with Cobalion and Terrakion to protect the Pokémon of the Unova region.

cards.name: Radiant Tsareena
cards.flavorText: This feared Pokémon has long, slender legs and a cruel heart. It shows no mercy as it stomps on its opponents.

cards.name: Vulpix
cards.flavorText: While young, it has six gorgeous tails. When it grows, several new tails are sprouted.

cards.name: Ninetales
cards.flavorText: It is said to live 1,000 years, and each of its tails is loaded with supernatural powers.

cards.name: Growlithe
cards.flavorText: It has a brave and trustworthy nature. It fearlessly stands up to bigger and stronger foes.

cards.name: Arcanine
cards.flavorText: The sight of it running over 6,200 miles in a single day and night has captivated many people.

cards.name: Ponyta
cards.flavorText: It can't run properly when it's newly born. As it races around with others of its kind, its legs grow stronger.

cards.name: Rapidash
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon can be seen galloping through fields at speeds of up to 150 mph, its fiery mane fluttering in the wind.

cards.name: Victini
cards.flavorText: When it shares the infinite energy it creates, that being's entire body will be overflowing with power.

cards.name: Fennekin
cards.flavorText: As it walks, it munches on a twig in place of a snack. It intimidates opponents by puffing hot air out of its ears.

cards.name: Braixen
cards.flavorText: When the twig is plucked from its tail, friction sets the twig alight. The flame is used to send signals to its allies.

cards.name: Delphox
cards.flavorText: Using psychic power, it generates a fiery vortex of 5,400 degrees Fahrenheit, incinerating foes swept into this whirl of flame.

cards.name: Fletchinder
cards.flavorText: Fletchinder launches embers into the den of its prey. When the prey comes leaping out, Fletchinder's sharp talons finish it off.

cards.name: Talonflame
cards.flavorText: Talonflame mainly preys upon other bird Pokémon. To intimidate opponents, it sends embers spewing from gaps between its feathers.

cards.name: Litten
cards.flavorText: Its coat regrows twice a year. When the time comes, Litten sets its own body on fire and burns away the old fur.

cards.name: Torracat
cards.flavorText: When its mane is standing on end, you can tell it's feeling good. When it isn't feeling well, its fur will lie down flat.

cards.name: Incineroar
cards.flavorText: When its fighting spirit is set alight, the flames around its waist become especially intense.

cards.name: Articuno
cards.flavorText: It's said that this Pokémon's beautiful blue wings are made of ice. Articuno flies over snowy mountains, its long tail fluttering along behind it.

cards.name: Wailmer
cards.flavorText: It shows off by spraying jets of seawater from the nostrils above its eyes. It eats a solid ton of Wishiwashi every day.

cards.name: Wailord
cards.flavorText: It can sometimes knock out opponents with the shock created by breaching and crashing its big body onto the water.

cards.name: Feebas
cards.flavorText: Although unattractive and unpopular, this Pokémon's marvelous vitality has made it a subject of research.

cards.name: Milotic
cards.flavorText: Milotic has provided inspiration to many artists. It has even been referred to as the most beautiful Pokémon of all.

cards.name: Snorunt
cards.flavorText: It's said that if they are seen at midnight, they'll cause heavy snow. They eat snow and ice to survive.

cards.name: Glalie
cards.flavorText: It has a body of ice that won't melt, even with fire. It can instantly freeze moisture in the atmosphere.

cards.name: Froslass
cards.flavorText: After a woman met her end on a snowy mountain, her regrets lingered on. From them, this Pokémon was born. Its favorite food is frozen souls.

cards.name: Relicanth
cards.flavorText: Rock-hard scales and oil-filled swim bladders allow this Pokémon to survive the intense water pressure of the deep sea.

cards.name: Phione
cards.flavorText: It drifts in warm seas. It always returns to where it was born, no matter how far it may have drifted.

cards.name: Keldeo
cards.flavorText: When it is resolute, its body fills with power and it becomes swifter. Its jumps are then too fast to follow.

cards.name: Dewpider
cards.flavorText: It forms a water bubble at the rear of its body and then covers its head with it. Meeting another Dewpider means comparing water-bubble sizes.

cards.name: Araquanid
cards.flavorText: It launches water bubbles with its legs, drowning prey within the bubbles. This Pokémon can then take its time to savor its meal.

cards.name: Pikachu
cards.flavorText: Pikachu that can generate powerful electricity have cheek sacs that are extra soft and super stretchy.

cards.name: Raichu
cards.flavorText: Its long tail serves as a ground to protect itself from its own high-voltage power.

cards.name: Chinchou
cards.flavorText: Its antennae, which evolved from a fin, have both positive and negative charges flowing through them.

cards.name: Lanturn
cards.flavorText: The light it emits is so bright that it can illuminate the sea's surface from a depth of over three miles.

cards.name: Rotom
cards.flavorText: One boy's invention led to the development of many different machines that take advantage of Rotom's unique capabilities.

cards.name: Emolga
cards.flavorText: As Emolga flutters through the air, it crackles with electricity. This Pokémon is cute, but it can cause a lot of trouble.

cards.name: Stunfisk
cards.flavorText: Thanks to bacteria that lived in the mud flats with it, this Pokémon developed the organs it uses to generate electricity.

cards.name: Zeraora
cards.flavorText: It approaches its enemies at the speed of lightning, then tears them limb from limb with its sharp claws.

cards.name: Radiant Alakazam
cards.flavorText: It has an incredibly high level of intelligence. Some say that Alakazam remembers everything that ever happens to it, from birth till death.

cards.name: Drowzee
cards.flavorText: It puts its prey to sleep and devours their dreams. It seems that bad dreams taste sour, so Drowzee doesn't particularly like eating them.

cards.name: Hypno
cards.flavorText: There are some Hypno that assist doctors with patients who can't sleep at night in hospitals.

cards.name: Jynx
cards.flavorText: In certain parts of Galar, Jynx was once feared and worshiped as the Queen of Ice.

cards.name: Misdreavus
cards.flavorText: What makes it happy is imitating the voices of weeping people and scaring everyone. It doesn't deal well with folks who aren't easily frightened.

cards.name: Mismagius
cards.flavorText: Its muttered curses can cause awful headaches or terrifying visions that torment others.

cards.name: Ralts
cards.flavorText: It is highly attuned to the emotions of people and Pokémon. It hides if it senses hostility.

cards.name: Kirlia
cards.flavorText: If its Trainer becomes happy, it overflows with energy, dancing joyously while spinning about.

cards.name: Gardevoir
cards.flavorText: It has the power to predict the future. Its power peaks when it is protecting its Trainer.

cards.name: Meditite
cards.flavorText: It eats just one berry a day. By enduring hunger, its spirit is tempered and made sharper.

cards.name: Medicham
cards.flavorText: Through yoga training, it gained the psychic power to predict its foe's next move.

cards.name: Chimecho
cards.flavorText: Emitting ultrasonic cries, it floats on winds to travel great distances.

cards.name: Sigilyph
cards.flavorText: Psychic power allows these Pokémon to fly. Some say they were the guardians of an ancient city. Others say they were the guardians' emissaries.

cards.name: Solosis
cards.flavorText: It communicates with others telepathically. Its body is encapsulated in liquid, but if it takes a heavy blow, the liquid will leak out.

cards.name: Duosion
cards.flavorText: Its psychic power can supposedly cover a range of more than half a mile—but only if its two brains can agree with each other.

cards.name: Reuniclus
cards.flavorText: While it could use its psychic abilities in battle, this Pokémon prefers to swing its powerful arms around to beat opponents into submission.

cards.name: Elgyem
cards.flavorText: If this Pokémon stands near a TV, strange scenery will appear on the screen. That scenery is said to be from its home.

cards.name: Beheeyem
cards.flavorText: Whenever a Beheeyem visits a farm, a Dubwool mysteriously disappears.

cards.name: Espurr
cards.flavorText: Though Espurr's expression never changes, behind that blank stare is an intense struggle to contain its devastating psychic power.

cards.name: Meowstic
cards.flavorText: Females are a bit more selfish and aggressive than males. If they don't get what they want, they will torment you with their psychic abilities.

cards.name: Swirlix
cards.flavorText: It eats its own weight in sugar every day. If it doesn't get enough sugar, it becomes incredibly grumpy.

cards.name: Slurpuff
cards.flavorText: By taking in a person's scent, it can sniff out their mental and physical condition. It's hoped that this skill will have many medical applications.

cards.name: Dedenne
cards.flavorText: A Dedenne's whiskers pick up electrical waves other Dedenne send out. These Pokémon share locations of food or electricity with one another.

cards.name: Indeedee
cards.flavorText: These intelligent Pokémon touch horns with each other to share information between them.

cards.name: Dreepy
cards.flavorText: After being reborn as a ghost Pokémon, Dreepy wanders the areas it used to inhabit back when it was alive in prehistoric seas.

cards.name: Drakloak
cards.flavorText: It's capable of flying faster than 120 mph. It battles alongside Dreepy and dotes on them until they successfully evolve.

cards.name: Dragapult
cards.flavorText: When it isn't battling, it keeps Dreepy in the holes on its horns. Once a fight starts, it launches the Dreepy like supersonic missiles.

cards.name: Phanpy
cards.flavorText: It is strong despite its compact size. It can easily pick up and carry an adult human on its back.

cards.name: Donphan
cards.flavorText: The longer and bigger its tusks, the higher its rank in its herd. The tusks take long to grow.

cards.name: Baltoy
cards.flavorText: It moves while spinning around on its single foot. Some Baltoy have been seen spinning on their heads.

cards.name: Claydol
cards.flavorText: This mysterious Pokémon started life as an ancient clay figurine made over 20,000 years ago.

cards.name: Anorith
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon was restored from a fossil. Anorith lived in the ocean about 100,000,000 years ago, hunting with its pair of claws.

cards.name: Armaldo
cards.flavorText: After evolution, this Pokémon emerged onto land. Its lower body has become stronger, and blows from its tail are devastating.

cards.name: Terrakion
cards.flavorText: It has phenomenal power. It will mercilessly crush anyone or anything that bullies small Pokémon.

cards.name: Hawlucha
cards.flavorText: It drives its opponents to exhaustion with its agile maneuvers, then ends the fight with a flashy finishing move.

cards.name: Sandygast
cards.flavorText: Grudges of the dead have possessed a mound of sand and become a Pokémon. Sandygast is fond of the shovel on its head.

cards.name: Palossand
cards.flavorText: Palossand is known as the Beach Nightmare. It pulls its prey down into the sand by controlling the sand itself, and then it sucks out their souls.

cards.name: Stonjourner
cards.flavorText: It stands in grasslands, watching the sun's descent from zenith to horizon. This Pokémon has a talent for delivering dynamic kicks.

cards.name: Zubat
cards.flavorText: It emits ultrasonic waves from its mouth to check its surroundings. Even in tight caves, Zubat flies around with skill.

cards.name: Golbat
cards.flavorText: It loves to drink other creatures' blood. It's said that if it finds others of its kind going hungry, it sometimes shares the blood it's gathered.

cards.name: Crobat
cards.flavorText: Both of its legs have turned into wings. Without a sound, Crobat flies swiftly toward its prey and sinks its fangs into the nape of its target's neck.

cards.name: Murkrow
cards.flavorText: It searches for shiny things for its boss. Murkrow's presence is said to be unlucky, so many people detest it.

cards.name: Honchkrow
cards.flavorText: Its goons take care of most of the fighting for it. The only time it dirties its own hands is in delivering a final blow to finish off an opponent.

cards.name: Croagunk
cards.flavorText: It makes frightening noises with its poison-filled cheek sacs. When opponents flinch, Croagunk hits them with a poison jab.

cards.name: Toxicroak
cards.flavorText: It bounces toward opponents and gouges them with poisonous claws. No more than a scratch is needed to knock out its adversaries.

cards.name: Sandile
cards.flavorText: The desert gets cold at night, so when the sun sets, this Pokémon burrows deep into the sand and sleeps until sunrise.

cards.name: Krokorok
cards.flavorText: Krokorok has specialized eyes that enable it to see in the dark. This ability lets Krokorok hunt in the dead of night without getting lost.

cards.name: Krookodile
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon is known as the Bully of the Sands. Krookodile's mighty jaws can bite through heavy plates of iron with almost no effort at all.

cards.name: Mareanie
cards.flavorText: The first symptom of its sting is numbness. The next is an itching sensation so intense that it's impossible to resist the urge to claw at your skin.

cards.name: Toxapex
cards.flavorText: To survive in the cold waters of Galar, this Pokémon forms a dome with its legs, enclosing its body so it can capture its own body heat.

cards.name: Morpeko
cards.flavorText: Intense hunger drives it to extremes of violence, and the electricity in its cheek sacs has converted into a Dark-type energy.

cards.name: Beldum
cards.flavorText: From its rear, Beldum emits a magnetic force that rapidly pulls opponents in. They get skewered on Beldum's sharp claws.

cards.name: Metang
cards.flavorText: Two Beldum have become stuck together via their own magnetic forces. With two brains, the resulting Metang has doubled psychic powers.

cards.name: Metagross
cards.flavorText: Because the magnetic powers of these Pokémon get stronger in freezing temperatures, Metagross living on snowy mountains are full of energy.

cards.name: Radiant Jirachi
cards.flavorText: It is said to have the ability to grant any wish for just one week every thousand years.

cards.name: Ferroseed
cards.flavorText: It defends itself by launching spikes, but its aim isn't very good at first. Only after a lot of practice will it improve.

cards.name: Ferrothorn
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon scrapes its spikes across rocks, and then uses the tips of its feelers to absorb the nutrients it finds within the stone.

cards.name: Klink
cards.flavorText: The two minigears that compose this Pokémon are closer than twins. They mesh well only with each other.

cards.name: Klang
cards.flavorText: When Klang goes all out, the minigear links up perfectly with the outer part of the big gear, and this Pokémon's rotation speed increases sharply.

cards.name: Klinklang
cards.flavorText: From its spikes, it launches powerful blasts of electricity. Its red core contains an enormous amount of energy.

cards.name: Cobalion
